assetStatus: Not yet built. This is a procedural-three model: generated at runtime from three.js primitives, not a GLB. `url` is a placeholder for the scene-builder module per project conventions. `thumbnailUrl` is a placeholder PNG. `defaultCamera`/`cameraDefault` and hotspot `position`s are estimates derived from the assetBrief — verify against the running scene before shipping.

hotspots.label: Great Red Spot
hotspots.description: A swirling storm on Jupiter wider than Earth, observed continuously for at least 190 years. The model shows it as a subtle oval indent in the banded surface.
hotspots.positionHint: Lower-left sphere (Jupiter, radius ~0.62), on the upper-left of the visible face — a slightly recessed flat oval with soft edge shading among the cream-and-tan bands, paired with a small Earth-reference disc floating beside it.
hotspots.function: Shows the solar system's biggest storm, scaled against an Earth reference.

hotspots.label: Olympus Mons
hotspots.description: The tallest volcano in the solar system — about 22 km high on Mars, nearly three times Mount Everest — a broad shield volcano built by lava flows.
hotspots.positionHint: Right-center sphere (Mars, radius ~0.4), a gently raised dome with a faint summit caldera ring on the upper-right of the face.
hotspots.function: Highlights the solar system's record volcano.

hotspots.label: Valles Marineris
hotspots.description: A canyon system over 4,000 km long on Mars — about the width of the United States — with depths several times the Grand Canyon's.
hotspots.positionHint: Same Mars sphere as Olympus Mons, lower area — a shallow V-shaped groove wrapping partway around the sphere's equator region.
hotspots.function: Marks the solar system's grandest canyon network.

hotspots.label: Saturn's rings
hotspots.description: Trillions of separate chunks of ice and rock — not solid sheets — orbiting Saturn, from dust grains to house-sized boulders.
hotspots.positionHint: Upper-center sphere (Saturn, radius ~0.45), the ring plane where the torus meets the planet — the hotspot sits on the inner edge of the main ring band.
hotspots.function: Marks the ring system and its orbiting-particle structure.

hotspots.label: Oceans and continents
hotspots.description: Earth is the only world known to have liquid water oceans on its surface, dividing its continents — the features we live on.
hotspots.positionHint: Lower-center sphere (Earth, radius ~0.3), an ocean-blue face with warm green-brown continent patches.
hotspots.function: Marks the only known life-bearing surface features.

hotspots.label: The Moon's maria
hotspots.description: The dark patches on the Moon's face — ancient plains of solidified lava that flooded impact basins billions of years ago.
hotspots.positionHint: Right side of the scene, a small grey sphere (radius ~0.15) with three darker grey-blue oval patches.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier quality bar throughout: warm off-white studio backdrop, no floor grid, no glow, no bloom, no emissive materials, no cartoon outlines. Six worlds float in a loose arc over a soft radial ground-shadow: Jupiter (upper-left), Saturn (upper-center), Mars (right-center), Earth (lower-center), the Moon (right), each at a comfortable reading size with landmark detail modeled as subtle surface relief (baked displacement, not decals). Landmark labels are slim text planes that appear on hotspot tap. A small Earth-reference disc floats beside the Great Red Spot to sell its size. Planet colors are the branch's muted set; hotspot dots are the only saturated accents. Auto-rotate is slow (~30s/rev) and pauses when a hotspot is open.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, roughness ~0.55-0.65. Surface detail (storm oval, dome, groove, ring banding, maria) modeled as baked vertex displacement or flat-shaded relief on the sphere geometry — no image textures, no emissive. Ring: a thin flat torus (two bands) in pale gold at low opacity. Labels: dark warm-grey text sprites. No emissive channels; app runtime handles highlight-on-tap.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: A 'world gallery' — six spheres arranged in a shallow arc on XZ: Jupiter (-1.6, 0.1, -0.2; radius 0.62), Saturn (-0.1, 0.2, 0.25; radius 0.45, plus ring torus radii 0.75/0.9 at tilt ~26°), Mars (1.7, -0.05, -0.1; radius 0.4), Earth (-0.7, -0.4, 0.4; radius 0.3), the Moon (1.2, 0.15, 0.6; radius 0.15). Feature relief: Great Red Spot — a shallow recessed oval (2:1 axis) on Jupiter's face, tinted a few percent away from the base banding; Olympus Mons — a low dome (radius 0.09, height 0.02) with a faint caldera ring; Valles Marineris — a shallow V-groove (0.35 long, 0.01 deep) wrapping the equator region of Mars; Saturn rings — thin two-band torus; Earth — baked ocean/continent two-tone relief; Moon maria — three low dark oval patches. An Earth-reference disc (radius 0.05, thin cylinder) floats near the Great Red Spot connected by a hairline. Landmark labels (name planes) toggle with hotspots. Camera default [0.4, 1.1, 4.6] → [0, 0.2, 0] shows all six worlds; tapping a hotspot eases the camera to that world (framing it at ~70% viewport height). Grounding: radial ground-shadow beneath the arc. Named groups per layers list.
